output.text: The morning fog lifted early over the shoreline as volunteers gathered near the boardwalk for the annual beach clean-up. Otto arrived first, carrying two mesh bags and a trash grabber he had borrowed from his neighbor. Assume that Cleo is the head judge. Kira showed up a few minutes later, stretching after her jog along the pier, while Esme trailed behind with a wagon full of empty buckets. Leo arrived last of the five, still buttoning his jacket against the wind. The volunteers were split into small teams to cover different sections of sand, and each team was given a colored flag to mark its zone. Otto finished ahead of Kira. Cleo had organized the flags by color the night before, matching them to a map taped inside the registration tent. Kira finished ahead of Esme. The tide was unusually low that day, exposing a wide stretch of sand littered with bottle caps and tangled fishing line. Leo won the raffle. Esme spent extra time near the rocks, untangling a length of rope that had washed up with the seaweed. Otto finished ahead of Esme. By early afternoon, the group had filled more bags than expected, and someone suggested doing this every month instead of once a season. Kira mentioned she was two years older than Leo, though nobody seemed surprised. As the sun dipped lower, the volunteers gathered their equipment, folded the flags, and walked back toward the parking lot together, satisfied with the clean stretch of shoreline behind them.”
